title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index (July 2027), 10:00 a.m. ET
source: EST: the publisher's standing rule, restated on conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200) -- "The Conference Board publishes the Consumer Confidence Index (R) at 10 a.m. ET on the last Tuesday of every month." 2027-07-27 is the last Tuesday of July 2027. The rule is corroborated for JULY specifically by three of the publisher's own dated next-release lines, each read off a June edition fetched direct 2026-09-06 at HTTP 200 and verified against its own "Source: June <year> Consumer Confidence Survey" line and "Updated:" stamp: CCI-June-2022 (Updated 2022-06-28) "The next release is Tuesday, July 26 at 10 AM ET", CCI-June-2023 (2023-06-27) "Tuesday, July 25", CCI-June-2024 (2024-06-25) "Tuesday, July 30th" -- each of which is the last Tuesday of its July. No July-2027 announcement exists yet, so this is the publisher's rule applied forward against a verified July record rather than a posted date. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED during the consumer-confidence-2027-06-29 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06), one edition forward on the same chain. Proposed for one measured reason: IT IS AN FOMC DAY-ONE COLLISION, and the direct within-year replication of the 04-27 collision print. The Fed's posted calendar (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, fetched 2026-09-06 HTTP 200, 164,831 bytes) puts the July 2027 meeting at 07-27/28, and 2027-07-27 is independently the last Tuesday of July 2027 by weekday arithmetic -- so this edition prints at 10:00 a.m. on the morning the Committee convenes, exactly as 2027-04-27 does. That gives 2027 TWO collisions from one release rule, which no year in the 2021-2026 tape has: across the 68 rule-derived CB days in that window the split is 51 clean / 17 colliding, and every one of the 17 is a day-one with zero decision-day collisions. A lane taking this id should note what the 06-29 sibling measured about the collision class before re-deriving it: the clean-day null is 0 of 9 on all nine instruments (smallest p XLF 0.2713) and the April lane declined its own directional p=0.0183 for multiple comparisons. Note also that July's own cut-off lag is unmeasured -- the June editions give the July RELEASE dates but not July's cut-offs, and June's lags are 6/7/6 against May's 8/7/8, so the chain now knows the lag varies by month and should not be borrowed across months (the 06-29 lane's correction of its own proposer). Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
